stops.name: Mount of Temptation, Jericho, the forty days
stops.campa: The Spirit drives him up into the wilderness, into the barren hills above Jericho, where he fasts forty days and forty nights and is afterward hungry. The tempter comes: turn these stones to bread; cast thyself from the pinnacle of the Temple; fall down and worship me, and all the kingdoms of the world are thine. To each Jesus answers with the word of God, and refuses. Then the devil leaves him, and behold, angels come and minister unto him. The new Adam stands where the first Adam fell, and does not fall.
stops.quote: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

stops.name: Cana of Galilee, water into wine, the first sign
stops.campa: There is a marriage in Cana, and Jesus and his mother and disciples are called. The wine fails, and Mary tells him. His hour is not yet come, he says, yet at her word the servants fill six stone jars with water to the brim. Draw out now, he tells them, and bear to the governor of the feast. The water has become wine, the best wine, kept until last. This is the beginning of miracles; he manifests his glory, and his disciples believe on him. The first sign is joy poured out at a wedding, abundance where there was lack.
stops.quote: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.

stops.name: Sychar, the Samaritan woman at Jacob's Well
stops.campa: Wearied with the journey, he sits alone at Jacob's Well in Samaria at the sixth hour, and asks a woman come to draw, Give me to drink. She marvels that a Jew speaks to a Samaritan woman. He offers her living water, that whoever drinks of it shall never thirst but have a well springing up to everlasting life. He tells her all she ever did: five husbands, and he that she has now not her own; and she perceives he is a prophet. He reveals that God is Spirit and must be worshipped in spirit and truth, and to her, an outsider, he says plainly: I am he.
stops.quote: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

stops.name: Capernaum: the town of his own, and the calling of the Twelve
stops.campa: Leaving Nazareth, Jesus comes and dwells in Capernaum by the sea, and makes it his own city. Walking by the Sea of Galilee he sees Simon and Andrew casting a net, and James and John mending theirs, and calls them: Follow me. Straightway they leave nets and father and follow him. In the synagogue he teaches as one having authority, casts out an unclean spirit, and heals Peter's wife's mother of a fever; and at evening the whole town is gathered at the door, and he heals all their sick. From the twelve he calls, he makes apostles.
stops.quote: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

stops.name: Mount of Beatitudes, the Sermon on the Mount
stops.campa: Seeing the multitudes, he goes up into a mountain, and his disciples come, and he opens his mouth and teaches them. Blessed are the poor in spirit; blessed are they that mourn; blessed are the meek, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, the persecuted. He gives them the Lord's Prayer, tells them to love their enemies, to lay up treasure in heaven, to seek first the kingdom of God. The crowds are astonished, for he teaches with authority. On a green hillside above the lake, the new law is given, higher than Sinai's.
stops.quote: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

stops.name: Galilee, the cleansing of the leper
stops.campa: A leper comes to him, an outcast forbidden to draw near any man, and kneels down: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean. Moved with compassion, Jesus does what the law forbids: he puts forth his hand and touches him. I will; be thou clean. Immediately the leprosy departs, and the man is whole. The touch that should have defiled the healer instead heals the leper; uncleanness flows backward. Jesus charges him to show himself to the priest, but the man cannot keep silent, and the fame of it spreads through all the region.

stops.name: Nain, the raising of the widow's son
stops.campa: As he comes near the gate of the town of Nain, a dead man is carried out, the only son of his mother, and she a widow, and a great crowd of the town with her. When the Lord sees her, he has compassion on her and says, Weep not. He comes and touches the bier, and the bearers stand still, and he speaks to the corpse: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sits up and begins to speak, and Jesus delivers him to his mother. Fear seizes them all, and they glorify God, saying a great prophet is risen among us, and God has visited his people.
stops.quote: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

stops.name: Capernaum, the paralytic let down through the roof
stops.campa: The house is so thronged that no one can come near the door. Four men carry a paralytic on a bed, and finding no way in, they climb the roof, break it open, and let him down before Jesus. Seeing their faith he says, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee. The scribes murmur: who can forgive sins but God alone? To show he has that power, he turns to the man: Arise, take up thy bed, and walk. And immediately he rises, takes up his bed, and goes forth before them all, and they are amazed and glorify God.
stops.quote: Arise, take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

stops.name: The Sea of Galilee, the stilling of the storm
stops.campa: They put out across the lake at evening, and Jesus falls asleep in the stern on a pillow. A great tempest rises; the waves beat into the boat, and it fills, and the disciples are afraid. They wake him: Master, carest thou not that we perish? He arises, rebukes the wind, and says to the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceases, and there is a great calm. Then he asks them why they are so fearful, how it is they have no faith. And they fear exceedingly, saying one to another, What manner of man is this, that even wind and sea obey him?

stops.name: Kursi (Gergesa), the Gerasene demoniac
stops.campa: On the far shore, among the tombs, a man possessed of a legion of demons meets him: one whom no chains could bind, crying out and cutting himself with stones night and day. The demons fall down before Jesus and beg not to be sent into the abyss but into a herd of swine. He gives them leave; the unclean spirits enter the swine, and the whole herd, two thousand, run violently down the steep place into the sea and drown. The man is found sitting, clothed, in his right mind. He begs to follow; Jesus sends him home to tell what great things God has done.
stops.quote: Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee.

stops.name: Capernaum, the raising of Jairus's daughter
stops.campa: Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, falls at his feet: my little daughter lies at the point of death, come and lay thy hands on her. On the way a woman with a twelve-year issue of blood touches the hem of his garment and is healed, for virtue goes out of him. Then word comes that the girl is dead. Fear not, only believe, he tells the father. He puts out the mourners, takes her by the hand, and speaks. Talitha cumi: Damsel, arise. Straightway the girl of twelve rises and walks, and he bids them give her food. Her parents are astonished.
stops.quote: Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.

stops.name: Tabgha, the feeding of the five thousand
stops.campa: The multitude has followed him into a desert place, and evening comes with nothing to eat. Send them away, the disciples say. But he answers, Give ye them to eat. They have only five loaves and two fishes. He bids the people sit down on the green grass in ranks, takes the loaves, looks up to heaven, blesses and breaks them, and gives to the disciples to set before the crowd. All eat and are filled, about five thousand men, beside women and children, and they take up twelve baskets of fragments. From a boy's lunch, a feast for a nation.
stops.quote: They need not depart; give ye them to eat.
